theme: The park: people make the paths, and the keeper watches where they walk before anyone paves. Taken from the essay's own line, "Learn where people walk before deciding where to pave."
cast: THE KEEPER, the recurring hero: a small, round, fuzzy park-keeper creature with a peaked ranger cap, one tuft of hair poking out of it, huge mismatched round eyes, a pencil behind one ear, a clipboard and a little hand-held tally counter on a cord; endlessly curious and delighted by what people do. THE PLANNERS: tall, lanky creatures in short-sleeved shirts with small ties and lanyards, carrying rolled blueprints and rulers; earnest and a little pompous. THE TINKERERS: scrappy, energetic creatures with welding goggles pushed up on their heads, tool belts and rolled sleeves. THE EVERYDAY FOLK: soft, cosy, cautious creatures in cardigans and knitted hats, with handbags, teacups and the odd pram.

images.name: the-two-gardens
images.subject: Two neighbouring allotment gardens divided by a low picket fence. LEFT: a planner stands on a stepladder proudly polishing a colossal, gleaming, ornate watering can as big as a car, with a prize rosette on it, over a perfectly raked, perfectly empty bed in which one tiny sprout droops. RIGHT: a scruffy, overflowing garden bursting with odd, wonderful, mismatched plants. Tinkerers poke seeds into unlikely places (a boot, a teapot, a wheelbarrow). The keeper walks a well-worn circular footpath that loops round the garden past seed packets, the beds, a pinned-up hand-drawn chart on a stake and a compost bin stuffed with old notes, carrying only a small dented old watering can and stopping to tick his clipboard as a sprout opens. The loop of footprints is clearly visible. A few everyday folk lean on the fence, admiring the right-hand garden.
images.alt: A planner polishes a giant prize-winning watering can over an empty bed, while next door a park keeper with a small dented can walks a worn loop round a garden bursting with plants, noting what grows.

images.name: the-tea-tray
images.subject: On a park path, an everyday-folk creature smugly carries a single teacup on a saucer, perfectly steady, not a drop spilt, but it is only one cup. Beside it a tinkerer on a wobbly unicycle tries to carry an enormous towering stack: a whole tea service, a teapot, a three-tier cake, a vase of flowers, a suitcase, a folded paper fan and a little paper lantern, all balanced on a tray on one hand; the tower leans dramatically, one cup already flying off with motion lines and a splash. The keeper stands between them with a tape measure and his clipboard, studying how high the stack can go before it falls.
images.alt: One creature carries a single teacup perfectly steadily while another wobbles on a unicycle under a towering stack of a whole tea service, cake and suitcase that is starting to fall, and the park keeper measures it.

images.name: the-relay
images.subject: A long line of eight creatures passing a magnificent tall layered birthday cake hand to hand from left to right, like a bucket chain across a park lawn. Each handover goes only a little wrong: one creature sneezes on it, the next pokes a finger in the icing, the next trips over a root, the next takes a sneaky bite, the next tilts it, a bird pecks the cherry, the next drops a layer. At the far right, the eighth creature proudly presents a plate holding a few crumbs and one bent candle to a hungry everyday-folk customer, whose face falls. The cake visibly shrinks and gets messier from left to right.
images.alt: Eight creatures pass a tall cake down a line; each handover goes slightly wrong, and the last proudly presents a plate of crumbs and a bent candle to a disappointed customer.

images.name: the-desire-path
images.after: Product-market fit for AI has to play out bottom-up
images.subject: A park lawn seen from slightly above. The planners' elegant paved path curls in grand swirls and loops round a flowerbed, past an ornate signpost, completely deserted. Straight across the grass, a muddy, worn shortcut has been trodden by a steady stream of creatures: everyday folk with handbags, a tinkerer pushing a wheelbarrow, someone with a pram, one skipping. A planner stands on the empty paved path holding a blueprint, scandalised. The keeper sits up in a tree beside the shortcut with binoculars round his neck, delightedly clicking his tally counter and ticking each walker on his clipboard.
images.alt: A grand, swirling paved path lies empty while a stream of creatures has worn a straight shortcut across the grass, and the park keeper counts them from a tree.

images.name: the-cardboard-box
images.after: None of these were planned features.
images.subject: A tinkerer hands out plain, identical cardboard boxes from a tall stack. All around, creatures have turned their boxes into things nobody planned: a filing cabinet with neatly labelled drawers stuffed with papers, a boat sailing in a puddle, a painter's easel with a canvas, a trap catching a startled beetle under a propped-up box with a stick and string, a knight's helmet, and a little conveyor belt of boxes passing tidy parcels along. A planner holds up the box's original design drawing, which shows only a plain box, and stares around in astonishment. The keeper runs between them, sketching each new use; sheets of drawings overflow from his clipboard.
images.alt: A tinkerer hands out plain cardboard boxes and creatures turn them into a filing cabinet, a boat, an easel and a beetle trap, while a planner stares and the park keeper sketches every new use.

images.name: paving-the-path
images.subject: The same worn shortcut across the park lawn, now being paved. A road crew of planners in hard hats lays neat paving stones exactly along the wobbly trodden line, following its footprints and kinks faithfully, and adds a bench, a handrail and a lamp post. The keeper walks ahead marking the route with chalk from his clipboard notes. Everyday folk with handbags, teacups and a pram stroll happily along the freshly paved part. Far ahead, past the end of the new paving, tinkerers are already trampling a fresh, faint new trail up into the hills.
images.alt: Road builders pave exactly along a trodden shortcut while everyday folk stroll on the finished part, and tinkerers are already trampling a new trail into the hills ahead.

images.name: the-roundabout
images.after: Give power users a raw tool
images.subject: A playground roundabout spinning fast, with curved speed lines and a deep circular groove worn into the ground round it. Tinkerers in goggles run alongside, pushing it round. Everyday folk sit on it comfortably, waving, holding teacups and hats, one with a knitting bag. One rider points and calls out to the keeper, who stands at the edge noting the request, and hands the note to a tinkerer-mechanic who, mid-spin, is bolting a bigger, sturdier seat with a backrest onto the roundabout. Everything is in motion and joyful.
images.alt: Tinkerers push a spinning playground roundabout full of happy riders while the park keeper takes a rider's request to a mechanic bolting on a bigger seat as it turns.

images.name: the-tested-bridge
images.after: That's why trust in a vendor isn't enough.
images.subject: A rickety rope bridge over a ravine in the park. Tinkerers on it jump, stomp and bounce to test it, hammering in patched planks and fresh nails. Behind them, a calm line of everyday folk crosses carrying teacups, stepping only on the well-trodden planks covered in footprints. On the near side, a planner proudly holds up a big ornate certificate with a wax seal and a ribbon, gesturing to a different, shiny but untested side bridge, where one everyday creature who took it now dangles from a snapped plank, eyes huge. The keeper stands at the head of the trusted bridge, clipboard in hand, waving people across.
images.alt: Tinkerers stomp-test a rope bridge so everyday folk can cross it calmly, while a planner waves a sealed certificate at a shiny untested bridge from which one creature dangles.

images.name: the-treehouse
images.subject: In an open meadow, dozens of creatures build a huge, wonky, wonderful treehouse together: ladders, rope pulleys hauling buckets, everyone adding a plank or a window, a rope bridge to a second tree, little flags, and a suggestion box nailed to the trunk, overflowing with notes. On the other side of a tall brick office wall, a lone planner sits at a desk under a stack of paperwork and rubber stamps, holding a single neat blueprint of a tidy small treehouse, standing on tiptoe on his chair to peer enviously over the wall.
images.alt: Dozens of creatures build a huge wonky treehouse together in an open meadow, while behind an office wall a lone planner with a neat blueprint and a pile of paperwork peers over enviously.

images.subject: PANEL 1: a tinkerer has improvised a wild new slide from a stepladder, an upside-down bathtub, an umbrella and a coil of hosepipe; a queue of delighted creatures waits to try it, one whooshing down. PANEL 2: the keeper measures the contraption carefully with a tape measure and draws an exact, tidy plan of it on his clipboard while the tinkerer looks on proudly. PANEL 3: in a neat workshop, planners stamp out identical, tidy slide kits from the keeper's plan and pack them into flat boxes on a conveyor; in the background, through the window, the tinkerer is already building something even stranger out of a canoe and a pram.
images.alt: A three-panel comic: a tinkerer improvises a slide from a ladder and bathtub; the keeper draws an exact plan of it; a workshop stamps out identical slide kits while the tinkerer builds something stranger.

images.name: inside-the-walls
images.subject: The courtyard of a big office building, enclosed by high walls, turned into a lively playground. Office creatures with lanyards, both tinkerers and everyday folk in cardigans, try out odd homemade contraptions: a swing made of an office chair, a seesaw from a whiteboard, a slide down the fire escape. The keeper sits high on a lifeguard's chair, clipboard and tally counter busy. At a small gate in the wall, two planners carefully pass a polished, proven version of the office-chair swing through to the public park outside, where a family of everyday folk waits, cheering.
images.alt: Behind an office's high walls, staff test homemade playground contraptions while the park keeper watches from a lifeguard chair, and a proven swing is passed out through a gate to a cheering family.

images.name: the-copycat
images.subject: LEFT: a planner-like rival in a tie has built an exact, shiny replica of the playground roundabout, polished to a gleam, behind a velvet rope and a cut ribbon, with a magnifying glass and a photo of the original in hand. It stands completely still and nobody is on it. RIGHT, over a low fence: the original scruffy roundabout spins full of laughing riders pushed by tinkerers, and it has already grown new things the copy lacks: a little canopy, a second ring of seats, a bell and a flag. The keeper rides along on it, clipboard out. The copier looks from the photo to the original, baffled.
images.alt: A rival has built a gleaming, perfect copy of the playground roundabout that stands still and empty, while over the fence the original spins full of riders and has already grown a canopy and new seats.
